poisson_blend — COLORTRANSPORT blend op

• Data kinds: image2d × image2d × mask → image2d

• Call: import fullseye as fs; fs.ledger.poisson_blend(src, dst, mask, offset=(0, 0)) (to call the implementation directly, import colortransport; colortransport.poisson_blend(src, dst, mask, offset=(0, 0)); from the registry, opscolortransport.get("poisson_blend"))

• Return value through the ledger: fullseye.ledger.poisson_blend(...) returns only the declared out type image2d (the underlying function also returns auxiliary values). When you need what was dropped, use fullseye.ledger.poisson_blend.raw(...) or call colortransport.poisson_blend directly.

Usage

Seamless compositing that carries the gradient field (Pérez, Gangnet & Blake, SIGGRAPH 2003).

Inside mask it keeps the gradient of src and solves for the image that equals the values of dst on the boundary. Hence the output satisfies the following 2 properties by construction, and that serves as a cross-check of correctness:

• the Laplacian inside matches the Laplacian of src (up to the residual of the solve)

• outside the mask it matches dst exactly (not 1 pixel is touched)

The colour of the pasted object changes. That is the purpose of the operation, but if you feed it as-is into a use such as "measure the colour of the pasted object", what you measure is the colour of the destination. The return value is (blended, info), and info["changed_pixels"] and info["max_shift"] tell how much actually moved.

Parameters

src : array_like

The picture to paste. (H, W) or (H, W, C).

dst : array_like

The destination. At least as large as src.

mask : array_like

Boolean of the same (H, W) as src. It must not touch the border

(explicitly rejected, because the boundary condition cannot be taken).

offset : (int, int)

(row, col) at which the top-left of src is placed within dst.

Returns

(ndarray, dict)
